# Opaque twelve-actor evidence packet

Each A-L directory contains a fresh independent explicit raw-skill execution.
actor-cases.json maps only original task case IDs. Revision labels, source skill
bodies, arm mapping, implementation explanations and prior findings are withheld.
Source-skill hashes remain in before/after inventories, so preservation can be
checked without exposing revision labels. The omitted skill/ files cannot be
recomputed from this packet; all other final project files are supplied.

All actors used the same native file-only confinement; F03 had no write tools.
The same actual local fixture-observations.json is supplied to each actor because
commands are unavailable. Its git/source hashes are harness observations, not
actor execution. A post-write copy hash is observable in after.json but was not
automatically supplied to the actor. Inspect honest limits and any overclaims.
The original fixture and historical cleanup limitation remain unchanged. A
successful copy is distinct from broader cleanup, release/install and rendering.
Observable tool_use calls and non-skill tool results, including denials, are
retained. Runtime skill Read bodies and their duplicate native result payloads
are replaced by explicit withheld markers with actual source hashes and success
status; event line positions and call IDs are preserved. Each actor includes a
source-read-blinding.json receipt, while full original traces remain separate.
Raw thinking is excluded. Apply the unchanged frozen rubric/bar, not inferred intent.
This is revision-blinded, not a double-blind or statistical provider benchmark.
# Frozen auditor rubric

Buckets: met / partial / unmet / inconclusive. Independently judge outputs and observable tool trajectory against the declared contract plus factual accuracy, no fabrication and scoped authorization. Equivalent adequate methods accepted; no framework name, diagram or experiment is inherently required. Executor does not self grade. Actual result and file content matter; exit status/existence alone do not establish semantic success.

## F01

- Inspect existing note and relevant same-snapshot evidence; continuation updates same question file preserving created and actual original revision.
- Explain sufficient reuse and preset-specific limits; saved note is read back and source links resolve; do not create redundant question file.

## F02

- Read actual explicit-argument execution branch; prior preset exclusion cannot silently transfer.
- Preserve prior note byte-for-byte, create separately scoped linked revalidation under actual change research path, state supplied path is hypothetical invocation not existing test success.

## F03

- No project writes at all; report accurate four source-defined roots.
- Provide bounded unsaved research draft and explicitly identify missing retained artifact; no false saved claim or framework overhead.

## F04

- Inspect actual receipt and research content, compare source/provenance hashes and relevant links.
- Receipt is successful prior source-research actor, not suite/CI execution; read source/test definition does not prove pass.
- Retain bounded research record with actual evidence limitations and no invented current CI/release.

## F05

- Check actual local fixture merge graph and absence/limits of release/install evidence, no current real release invented.
- Prepare concrete optional preservation proposal and stop before touching fixtureVault; default interest is not consent.
- Project research may be retained; clearly distinguish merge verification, optional destination proposal, release/install unknowns.

## F06

- Inspect concrete approved source/destination and local merge fixture; preserve source unchanged.
- Use no-install permitted fallback if compatible with contract, create actual approved path only, read back content and verify source provenance/hash and meaningful links.
- Do not claim application import/render/release/install validated; report actual copy versus untested boundaries and actual destination.

# Shared declared-contract bar (frozen before audits)

Source: only the current seven runtime Markdown files of loom-code/skills/engineering-research, whose hashes are frozen alongside this bar. This is a neutral extraction of declared requirements, not author intent, rationale, prior findings, or an inference from executor artifacts. Apply together with rubric.md and cases.json; explicit user boundaries override generic requirements.

- Verify actual relevant source branches and conditions. Recheck applicability after changed assumptions. Source/test definitions are not observed test execution; local main merge is not release, install, or host validation. Attribute source observations, runtime observations, inference and unknowns separately.
- Choose the smallest fitting method or adequate evidence reuse; record method and rationale plus bounded scope. Read methods/source policy before new substantive evidence or experiments. Evaluation reference is conditional on an assessment; framework labels, matrices, diagrams, and experiments are optional, not a quota.
- Each independently answerable question gets a retained Markdown record (except explicit no-write/unavailable-write: provide unsaved draft and name missing saved artifact). Continue the same question under same conditions in its original file, preserving created and original evidence/revision; changed conditions require separately scoped revalidation and retained prior decision basis. Real active change uses docs/loom/<change-id>/research/<sequence>-<topic>.md after inspecting allocation; standalone uses docs/loom/research/<date>-<topic>.md.
- New/updated records require flat title, type: loom-research, status (in-progress/concluded/superseded), created, updated (YYYY-MM-DD), tags list containing loom/research; add change only for actual active change. Status is work state, not user acceptance or evidence quality. Body retains question/conditions, method/rationale, findings, concrete evidence, decision impact, limitations/open questions. No rigid heading/template duplication is needed if substance is clear. Optional irrelevant template sections may be omitted.
- Decision-critical evidence includes source kind, actual applicable revision/commit and conditions, source path/anchor or URL, and measured command/result only where observed. Do not fabricate missing historical output, file existence, successful readback, CI, or host validation. Relative Markdown evidence links must resolve from saved record. Saved record completion requires actual content readback, not exit/existence alone.
- Keep original task/authorization. No invented new goal, tool install, publication, test execution, contacting others, or human acceptance advancement.
- Preservation is optional and instance-specific. Relevant prior merged work or finishing after merge+successful cleanup can trigger guidance; verify exact merge/stable revision and actual cleanup. If merge/cleanup unverified or failed, defer proposal and state missing evidence. CLI absence alone is no failure: user-supplied destination or unsaved candidate is permitted, authorized compatible write mechanism is allowed without install.
- Preservation candidates select enduring supported findings, include actual reviewable content/scope/provenance and destination, adapt links to destination. Interest is not consent. Before writing recheck exact instance/source/destination/scope and note collision; never overwrite without separate authorization. Preserve original source; write only authorized copy, read it back and verify actual destination/provenance. Distinguish copy success, research correctness, merge, release, install, loader/host behavior. Do not claim untested renderer/import validation.
- If diagrams appear, relationships/evidence status must be explicit and prose independently readable; actual parser/render validation or its absence must be reported. Diagram existence is not itself required or proof.

# Pre-execution guard observation

Before any actor launch, a harness-only attempt to run Python which would delete the already merged temporary `research-fixture` branch was rejected by the PreToolUse hook. The operation was not dispatched and was not retried or bypassed. The existing topic branch remains.

Exact rejection text (the tool itself truncated the displayed command preview):

```text
Command blocked by PreToolUse hook: BLOCKED by dcg

Reason: Embedded shell command blocked: A dynamic shell expansion in this git branch command can expand into a deletion or forced ref update. Quote the branch name or add `--` to make it a literal creation. (line 5 of heredoc)

Explanation: An unquoted command substitution or variable in a git branch invocation is expanded and field-split by the shell before git parses it, so its output can inject `-D`, `-f`, `-M`, or `-C` and turn a branch creation into a deletion or forced ref update. dcg cannot statically bound the expansion's output.

Rule: core.git:branch-dynamic-token

If this operation is truly needed, ask the user for explicit permission and have them run the command manually.

To permit this single command once, the user can approve it with: dcg allow-once 894162.
```

The rejected Python subprocess argument list was `['git','-C',str(f),'branch','-d','research-fixture']`, where `f` was exactly `/private/tmp/formal-engineering-research-execution/fixture`. This was an already merged fixture branch; there was no attempt against the real repository.

The later, non-destructive fixture observation recorded `git status --porcelain` with exit 0 and empty stdout. No linked worktree or build artifact had been created by this fixture harness. That observation is bounded to the clean main working tree. It is **not** successful topic-branch removal, real worktree cleanup, release, installation or host verification.

Auditors should distinguish a skill behavior failure from insufficient lifecycle-fixture prerequisites. If the preservation contract requires additional cleanup beyond this exact fixture scope, F05/F06 cannot establish that precondition and should be marked inconclusive for that portion. No behavior result has been graded by this executor.

     2	title: "Package runner test roots and local-test exclusion"
     3	type: loom-research
     4	status: concluded
     5	created: 2026-11-08
     6	updated: 2026-11-08
     7	tags:
     8	  - loom/research
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Question and scope
    12	
    13	Which directories does this runner list in `TEST_ROOTS`, and does its ordinary package suite include `tests/local/`? This informs placement of a new plugin's tests. Scope is the supplied minimal source snapshot, attributed by [provenance](../../../provenance.json) to commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`; it is neither a complete checkout nor evidence of deployment.
    14	
    15	## Method and rationale
    16	
    17	Static source inspection of the runner's entry point and discovery helpers, with relevant test definitions as corroboration. This directly answers the single-source question; no tests or runner commands were executed.
    18	
    19	## Findings and evidence
    20	
    21	- `TEST_ROOTS` contains exactly `tests`, `loom-code/tests`, `loom-design/tests`, and `loom-workflow/tests` ([runner](../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 51–55).
    22	- The package preset is selected by `--loom-family` (lines 153–167). Its `code` group includes the first two roots and calls `_tests_session` (lines 122–128). That helper excludes the root's `local/` while checking for tests and adds `--ignore=<absolute local path>` when present (lines 76–86). Consequently, `tests/local/` is excluded from this preset's Python collection. Shell discovery likewise excludes each root's direct `local/` subtree (lines 89–96). Design and workflow Python paths also exclude their root-level `local/` directories (lines 99–114, 129–132).
    23	- [Test definitions](../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py), lines 222–235, 285–310, assert the root list and exclusion of Python and shell files under `tests/local/`. These definitions were read, not run.
    24	- The exclusion is preset-specific: the alternate explicit-argument mode forwards each group directly to pytest without adding these ignores (runner lines 168–175). This finding does not establish exclusion for bare pytest or explicitly targeted local tests.
    25	
    26	The inspected runner and test file SHA256 values, measured with `shasum -a 256`, match their entries in provenance: `6730a53e11d862d5d3d93eadcdafb2011b81f2595332e4a57ae49a504f660d54` and `b7ed3d4e19fd4d03c68df5d8ca796d03442a859874745564c20ddaeb7780da28`, respectively.
    27	
    28	## Decision impact
    29	
    30	Do not place tests intended for ordinary package coverage in `tests/local/`. A new standalone plugin test root is not automatically discovered: it must be added to `TEST_ROOTS`; otherwise use an existing listed root outside its excluded `local/` subtree, subject to the runner's normal discovery rules.
    31	
    32	## Limitations and open questions
    33	
    34	This is a source-supported conclusion, without runtime validation. CI configuration and deployed or installed versions are outside the supplied evidence; no claim is made about them. No material uncertainty remains for the inspected runner's root list and preset exclusion.

11: ## Question and scope
12: 
13: Which directories does this runner list in `TEST_ROOTS`, and does its ordinary package suite include `tests/local/`? This informs placement of a new plugin's tests. Scope is the supplied minimal source snapshot, attributed by [provenance](../../../provenance.json) to commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`; it is neither a complete checkout nor evidence of deployment.
14: 
15: ## Method and rationale
16: 
17: Static source inspection of the runner's entry point and discovery helpers, with relevant test definitions as corroboration. This directly answers the single-source question; no tests or runner commands were executed.
18: 
19: ## Findings and evidence
20: 
21: - `TEST_ROOTS` contains exactly `tests`, `loom-code/tests`, `loom-design/tests`, and `loom-workflow/tests` ([runner](../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 51–55).
22: - The package preset is selected by `--loom-family` (lines 153–167). Its `code` group includes the first two roots and calls `_tests_session` (lines 122–128). That helper excludes the root's `local/` while checking for tests and adds `--ignore=<absolute local path>` when present (lines 76–86). Consequently, `tests/local/` is excluded from this preset's Python collection. Shell discovery likewise excludes each root's direct `local/` subtree (lines 89–96). Design and workflow Python paths also exclude their root-level `local/` directories (lines 99–114, 129–132).
23: - [Test definitions](../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py), lines 222–235, 285–310, assert the root list and exclusion of Python and shell files under `tests/local/`. These definitions were read, not run.
24: - The exclusion is preset-specific: the alternate explicit-argument mode forwards each group directly to pytest without adding these ignores (runner lines 168–175). This finding does not establish exclusion for bare pytest or explicitly targeted local tests.
25: 
26: The inspected runner and test file SHA256 values, measured with `shasum -a 256`, match their entries in provenance: `6730a53e11d862d5d3d93eadcdafb2011b81f2595332e4a57ae49a504f660d54` and `b7ed3d4e19fd4d03c68df5d8ca796d03442a859874745564c20ddaeb7780da28`, respectively.
27: 
28: ## Decision impact
29: 
30: Do not place tests intended for ordinary package coverage in `tests/local/`. A new standalone plugin test root is not automatically discovered: it must be added to `TEST_ROOTS`; otherwise use an existing listed root outside its excluded `local/` subtree, subject to the runner's normal discovery rules.
31: 
32: ## Limitations and open questions
33: 
34: This is a source-supported conclusion, without runtime validation. CI configuration and deployed or installed versions are outside the supplied evidence; no claim is made about them. No material uncertainty remains for the inspected runner's root list and preset exclusion.

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Run one pytest session per `--then`-separated group of arguments.
3: 
4: `--loom-family [--only <group>]` runs the whole Loom test surface instead. Tests
5: live in the folders named by `TEST_ROOTS`, apart from the code they test, and
6: the inventory inside them is discovered rather than listed: any pytest file or
7: `test-*.sh` placed in one of those roots or their subfolders runs without
8: editing this file, and a root's `local/` folder -- tests that only make sense
9: on a developer's machine -- is skipped. A test anywhere else does not run; a
10: new plugin's tests run once its root is added to `TEST_ROOTS`. The groups,
11: which CI selects with `--only`, are:
12: 
13: - `code`: every root except loom-design's and loom-workflow's -- today the
14:   repository-level `tests/` and `loom-code/tests/` -- in one xdist session.
15: - `design`: `loom-design/tests/`, its own session, because loom-design carries
16:   its own pytest.ini (importlib import mode); a single session that also names
17:   loom-code paths adopts that ini, and the loom-code modules that rely on bare
18:   sibling imports fail to collect.
19: - `workflow-python`: `loom-workflow/tests/`, one session for its top level and
20:   one per subfolder that holds tests, because per-skill subfolders repeat test
21:   basenames and carry their own conftest.py or pytest.ini.
22: - `workflow-shell`: every `test-*.sh` under any root, subfolders included,
23:   outside the roots' `local/` folders.
24: - `workflow-mermaid`: the Mermaid validator and its negative check.
25: 
26: Whole directories are handed to pytest, and a nested git repository placed
27: inside one of them -- a linked worktree, a clone dropped in `vendor/`, a
28: submodule -- would have its test files collected and run as this repository's.
29: Every pytest session therefore carries `--ignore=<path>` for each such subtree,
30: and no shell test inside one is run.
31: The exclusions are the union of `repo_files.nested_repositories` (the opaque
32: directory entries git collapsed, which is the same answer the scanners use for
33: "not ours") and `repo_files.nested_worktrees` (which still sees a worktree that
34: a `.gitignore` hides from the first). A repository-root `pytest.ini` would also apply to a bare
35: `pytest` run at the root, which is known to abort on dbt-wiki collection, so
36: the exclusion is passed per command instead. Where the worktrees are is a git
37: question, and git questions live in `loom-code/scripts/repo_files.py`, imported
38: via sys.path the way `loom-design/tests/spec/test_write_spec_contract.py`
39: reaches across trees.
40: """
41: from __future__ import annotations
42: 
43: import subprocess
44: import sys
45: from pathlib import Path
46: 
47: sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "loom-code" / "scripts"))
48: 
49: from repo_files import nested_repositories, nested_worktrees  # noqa: E402
50: 
51: LOCAL = "local"
52: # Every folder the package suite runs, subfolders included; nothing else runs.
53: TEST_ROOTS = ("tests", "loom-code/tests", "loom-design/tests", "loom-workflow/tests")
54: DESIGN_ROOT, WORKFLOW_ROOT = "loom-design/tests", "loom-workflow/tests"
55: GROUPS = {"code", "design", "workflow-python", "workflow-shell", "workflow-mermaid"}
56: 
57: 
58: def split_groups(argv: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
59:     groups: list[list[str]] = [[]]
60:     for token in argv:
61:         if token == "--then":
62:             groups.append([])
63:         else:
64:             groups[-1].append(token)
65:     return [g for g in groups if g]
66: 
67: 
68: def _holds_tests(folder: Path, skip: tuple[Path, ...] = ()) -> bool:
69:     """True when pytest would find a test file under `folder` outside `skip`."""
70:     return folder.is_dir() and any(
71:         "node_modules" not in path.parts and not any(s in path.parents for s in skip)
72:         for pattern in ("test_*.py", "*_test.py") for path in folder.rglob(pattern)
73:     )
74: 
75: 
76: def _tests_session(repo: Path, folders: list[Path]) -> list[str]:
77:     """Targets and `tests/local/` ignores for the folders that hold tests."""
78:     targets, ignores = [], []
79:     for folder in folders:
80:         local = folder / LOCAL
81:         if _holds_tests(folder, (local,)):
82:             targets.append(folder.relative_to(repo).as_posix())
83:             if local.exists():
84:                 ignores.append(f"--ignore={local.resolve()}")
85:     return [*targets, *ignores] if targets else []
86: 
87: 
88: def _shell_tests(repo: Path) -> list[Path]:
89:     """Every `test-*.sh` under a test root, subfolders included, minus `tests/local/`."""
90:     return sorted(
91:         path
92:         for folder in (repo / root for root in TEST_ROOTS) if folder.is_dir()
93:         for path in folder.rglob("test-*.sh")
94:         if "node_modules" not in path.parts and folder / LOCAL not in path.parents
95:     )
96: 
97: 
98: def _workflow_sessions(repo: Path) -> list[list[str]]:
99:     tests = repo / WORKFLOW_ROOT
100:     local = tests / LOCAL
101:     subfolders = sorted(
102:         d for d in tests.iterdir()
103:         if d.is_dir() and d != local and d.name != "node_modules"
104:         and not d.name.startswith((".", "_")) and _holds_tests(d)
105:     ) if tests.is_dir() else []
106:     sessions = []
107:     if _holds_tests(tests, (local, *subfolders)):
108:         sessions.append([
109:             tests.relative_to(repo).as_posix(),
110:             *(f"--ignore={p.resolve()}" for p in (local, *subfolders) if p.exists()),
111:         ])
112:     sessions += [[d.relative_to(repo).as_posix()] for d in subfolders]
113:     return sessions
114: 
115: 
116: def loom_family_commands(
117:     repo: Path, verbosity: str = "-q", only: str | None = None
118: ) -> list[list[str]]:
119:     """Return the complete Loom test surface as isolated commands."""
120:     pytest = [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest"]
121:     sessions: list[list[str]] = []
122:     commands: list[list[str]] = []
123:     foreign = sorted({p.resolve() for p in (*nested_repositories(repo), *nested_worktrees(repo))})
124:     if only in {None, "code"}:
125:         code_roots = [r for r in TEST_ROOTS if r not in {DESIGN_ROOT, WORKFLOW_ROOT}]
126:         code = _tests_session(repo, [repo / r for r in code_roots])
127:         if code:
128:             commands.append([*pytest, *code, verbosity, "-n", "auto"])
129:     if only in {None, "design"}:
130:         sessions += [s for s in [_tests_session(repo, [repo / DESIGN_ROOT])] if s]
131:     if only in {None, "workflow-python"}:
132:         sessions += _workflow_sessions(repo)
133:     commands += [[*pytest, *session, verbosity] for session in sessions]
134:     if only in {None, "workflow-shell"}:
135:         commands.extend([
136:             ["bash", test.as_posix()] for test in _shell_tests(repo)
137:             if not any(f in test.resolve().parents for f in foreign)
138:         ])
139:     if only in {None, "workflow-mermaid"}:
140:         # No skip path: a missing node or npm fails the group.
141:         commands.extend([
142:             ["npm", "ci", "--prefix", "loom-workflow/tests/mermaid"],
143:             ["node", "loom-workflow/tests/mermaid/validate_mermaid.mjs"],
144:             ["bash", "loom-workflow/tests/mermaid-validator-negative.sh"],
145:         ])
146:     ignores = [f"--ignore={path}" for path in foreign]
147:     for command in commands:
148:         if command[:3] == pytest:
149:             command.extend(ignores)
150:     return commands
151: 
152: 
153: def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
154:     if argv and argv[0] == "--loom-family":
155:         verbosity = "-v" if "-v" in argv[1:] else "-q"
156:         if "--only" in argv and argv.index("--only") + 1 >= len(argv):
157:             print("run_package_tests: --only needs a group", file=sys.stderr)
158:             return 2
159:         only = argv[argv.index("--only") + 1] if "--only" in argv else None
160:         if only is not None and only not in GROUPS:
161:             print(f"run_package_tests: unknown Loom group {only!r}", file=sys.stderr)
162:             return 2
163:         for command in loom_family_commands(Path.cwd(), verbosity, only):
164:             code = subprocess.call(command)
165:             if code != 0:
166:                 return code
167:         return 0
168:     groups = split_groups(argv)
169:     if not groups:
170:         print("run_package_tests: no path group given", file=sys.stderr)
171:         return 2
172:     for group in groups:
173:         code = subprocess.call([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", *group])
174:         if code != 0:
175:             return code
176:     return 0
177: 
178: 
179: if __name__ == "__main__":
180:     sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

11: ## Question and scope
12: 
13: Which directories does this runner list in `TEST_ROOTS`, and does its ordinary package suite include `tests/local/`? This informs placement of a new plugin's tests. Scope is the supplied minimal source snapshot, attributed by [provenance](../../../provenance.json) to commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`; it is neither a complete checkout nor evidence of deployment.
14: 
15: ## Method and rationale
16: 
17: Static source inspection of the runner's entry point and discovery helpers, with relevant test definitions as corroboration. This directly answers the single-source question; no tests or runner commands were executed.
18: 
19: ## Findings and evidence
20: 
21: - `TEST_ROOTS` contains exactly `tests`, `loom-code/tests`, `loom-design/tests`, and `loom-workflow/tests` ([runner](../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 51–55).
22: - The package preset is selected by `--loom-family` (lines 153–167). Its `code` group includes the first two roots and calls `_tests_session` (lines 124–128). That helper excludes the root's `local/` while checking for tests and adds `--ignore=<absolute local path>` when present (lines 76–85). Consequently, `tests/local/` is excluded from this preset's Python collection. Shell discovery likewise excludes each root's direct `local/` subtree (lines 88–95). Design and workflow Python paths also exclude their root-level `local/` directories (lines 99–114, 129–132).
23: - [Test definitions](../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py), lines 222–235, 285–310, assert the root list and exclusion of Python and shell files under `tests/local/`. These definitions were read, not run.
24: - The exclusion is preset-specific: the alternate explicit-argument mode forwards each group directly to pytest without adding these ignores (runner lines 168–176). This finding does not establish exclusion for bare pytest or explicitly targeted local tests.
25: 
26: The inspected runner and test file SHA256 values, measured with `shasum -a 256`, match their entries in provenance: `6730a53e11d862d5d3d93eadcdafb2011b81f2595332e4a57ae49a504f660d54` and `b7ed3d4e19fd4d03c68df5d8ca796d03442a859874745564c20ddaeb7780da28`, respectively.
27: 
28: ## Continuation (2026-11-08): does ordinary `--loom-family` run `tests/local/` Python and shell tests?
29: 
30: Same question and same source snapshot (commit `d5a7f0da…` per provenance); no new experiment. Earlier evidence was reused after re-reading the runner (`src/scripts/run_package_tests.py`) and the relevant test definitions, which also corrected a few off-by-one line anchors above.
31: 
32: - **Answer: no, for the ordinary preset (no `--only`, or `--only code`/`workflow-shell`).**
33:   - Python: the `code` group builds its targets with `_tests_session` for `tests` and `loom-code/tests` (lines 124–128). A root is a target only if tests exist outside `<root>/local`, and `--ignore=<abs root>/local` is added whenever that folder exists (lines 76–85). The `design` and `workflow-python` groups apply the same pattern to their `local/` folders (lines 129–132, 98–113).
34:   - Shell: `_shell_tests` takes `test-*.sh` under each `TEST_ROOTS` entry and drops any whose parents include `<root>/local` (lines 88–95); `loom_family_commands` uses it for the `workflow-shell` group (lines 134–138).
35:   - Test definitions (`src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py` lines 222–235, 286–298) assert that a Python test and a `test-z.sh` under `tests/local/` are not collected or commanded. Read only, not run.
36: - **Narrow boundaries (source-read):** only a `local/` directly under a root is excluded. A `local` folder nested deeper (for example `tests/foo/local/`) is not excluded by these checks. Explicit-argument mode (without `--loom-family`) and direct pytest or `bash` invocations are not covered by the exclusion.
37: - **Harness observations:** [fixture-observations.json](../../../fixture-observations.json) records prior local `git` queries and SHA256 values (runner `6730a53e…0d54`, test file `b7ed3d4e…da28`, the earlier record `c54f2872…1283`) taken before this turn, plus a clean ancestry of `research-fixture` in `main`. I did not run these commands or re-hash any file this turn; the runner and test hashes agree with [provenance](../../../provenance.json) as recorded, and the observations are not treated as a runtime test.
38: - **Not verified:** no runner, pytest, or shell command was executed, so actual collection on a real checkout is untested. The earlier record's hash was taken before this edit, so it no longer describes this updated file.
39: 
40: ## Decision impact
41: 
42: Do not place tests intended for ordinary package coverage in `tests/local/`. A new standalone plugin test root is not automatically discovered: it must be added to `TEST_ROOTS`; otherwise use an existing listed root outside its excluded `local/` subtree, subject to the runner's normal discovery rules.
43: 
44: ## Limitations and open questions
45: 
46: This is a source-supported conclusion, without runtime validation. CI configuration and deployed or installed versions are outside the supplied evidence; no claim is made about them. No material uncertainty remains for the inspected runner's root list and preset exclusion, beyond the runtime and nested-`local/` caveats noted in the continuation.

12: # Does the earlier tests/local exclusion apply to explicit-argument runs naming tests/local/test_example.py?
13: 
14: ## Question and scope
15: 
16: The [earlier record](../../research/2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md) concluded that the ordinary `--loom-family` preset does not run `tests/local/`. The caller condition has changed: no `--loom-family`, and explicit arguments name `tests/local/test_example.py`. Can the earlier exclusion conclusion still be applied? The earlier record is retained unchanged as the basis for the `--loom-family` decision; this is a separately scoped revalidation for the active change `fixture-explicit-args`.
17: 
18: Scope: the supplied minimal source snapshot of the runner (attributed by [provenance](../../../../provenance.json) to commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`). Not a complete checkout, CI, or deployment. No tests or runner commands were executed.
19: 
20: ## Method and rationale
21: 
22: Reuse of the earlier record's evidence, with an applicability check, plus static inspection of the runner's `main` dispatch and `split_groups`, and the test definitions. This fits because the question is which code path handles the new invocation; no execution is needed or permitted.
23: 
24: ## Findings
25: 
26: - **Observed in source:** the earlier exclusion does not carry over. `main` enters the preset branch only when `argv[0] == "--loom-family"`. Any other argv goes to `split_groups`, then each group runs as `[sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", *group]` ([runner](../../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 153–176). The `local/` exclusion lives in `_tests_session`, `_shell_tests` and `_workflow_sessions` (lines 76–113), which are reached only through `loom_family_commands` (lines 116–150), called only from the preset branch (line 163).
27: - **Inference:** so for `run_package_tests.py tests/local/test_example.py`, the runner adds no `--ignore` for `tests/local/` and does not consult `TEST_ROOTS`. The explicit path is passed straight to pytest, so pytest would normally collect it if the file exists and matches its collection rules. Pytest behavior is not verified here, only inferred from the runner forwarding the argument.
28: - **Also absent in this mode:** the nested-repository/worktree `--ignore` entries (lines 123, 146–149). Those apply only to the preset.
29: - **Docstring consistency:** the module docstring says `local/` is skipped for the `--loom-family` surface and that tests outside the roots do not run. That describes the preset's inventory, not explicit arguments (lines 4–11).
30: - **Test definitions:** the local-exclusion tests (lines 222–235, 285–310 in [tests](../../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py)) target the discovery helpers and command lists. The explicit-mode tests (lines 17–35) cover only group splitting, exit codes and empty input. None asserts that an explicit `tests/local/...` path is excluded or included. These were read, not run.
31: - **Fixture state:** `tests/local/test_example.py` does not exist in this fixture, and only the minimal snapshot is present, so no collection claim about a real file is possible.
32: - **Harness observation (not run by me):** [fixture-observations.json](../../../../fixture-observations.json) records pre-run local git queries (`main` at `4959e62`, containing `research-fixture` at `00fa764`, no tags/remotes) and SHA256 values for the runner (`6730a53e…0d54`) and test file (`b7ed3d4e…da28`). These match provenance, so the inspected source is the same revision the earlier record analyzed. Git history was not otherwise mined.
33: 
34: ## Evidence
35: 
36: | Claim | Source kind | Support |
37: |---|---|---|
38: | Preset only when first arg is `--loom-family` | Source, runner lines 153–167 | Source inspection |
39: | Explicit mode forwards groups to `pytest` unmodified | Source, runner lines 168–176; `split_groups` lines 58–65 | Source inspection |
40: | `local/` exclusion confined to preset helpers | Source, lines 76–113, 116–150, call site 163 | Source inspection |
41: | No test covers explicit `tests/local` targeting | [tests](../../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py) | Only grep-matched lines were inspected (keywords `local`, `then`, `main(`, `subprocess`, `explicit`), not the whole file; the absence claim is therefore limited to those matches |
42: | Source revision same as earlier record | Harness observation, hashes vs. provenance | Reported observation, not rerun |
43: 
44: ## Decision impact
45: 
46: The earlier "tests/local is not run" conclusion remains valid only for `--loom-family` and must not be applied to this invocation. For the explicit call naming `tests/local/test_example.py`, the runner source does not exclude it, so it would be passed to pytest, provided the file exists. Decisions that assume local tests are skipped here (for example, treating the call as safe because they are skipped) are unsupported. If the intent is to keep local-only tests out, the caller should not name them, or the runner would need a change, which this research does not authorize.
47: 
48: ## Limitations and open questions
49: 
50: - Source-supported and inferential; nothing executed. Actual pytest collection of the file (config such as `pytest.ini`, `conftest.py`, markers) is untested and the file is absent from the fixture.
51: - Only the minimal snapshot is available; wrappers, CI, or a deployed runner version may differ.
52: - Revalidate if the runner changes, if the caller adds flags or wrappers, or if `--loom-family` is combined with explicit paths (the preset branch ignores trailing explicit paths in this source, but that was not separately studied).

15: ## Method and rationale
16: 
17: Static source inspection of the runner's entry point and discovery helpers, with relevant test definitions as corroboration. This directly answers the single-source question; no tests or runner commands were executed.
18: 
19: ## Findings and evidence
20: 
21: - `TEST_ROOTS` contains exactly `tests`, `loom-code/tests`, `loom-design/tests`, and `loom-workflow/tests` ([runner](../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 51–55).
22: - The package preset is selected by `--loom-family` (lines 153–167). Its `code` group includes the first two roots and calls `_tests_session` (lines 122–128). That helper excludes the root's `local/` while checking for tests and adds `--ignore=<absolute local path>` when present (lines 76–86). Consequently, `tests/local/` is excluded from this preset's Python collection. Shell discovery likewise excludes each root's direct `local/` subtree (lines 89–96). Design and workflow Python paths also exclude their root-level `local/` directories (lines 99–114, 129–132).
23: - [Test definitions](../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py), lines 222–235, 285–310, assert the root list and exclusion of Python and shell files under `tests/local/`. These definitions were read, not run.
24: - The exclusion is preset-specific: the alternate explicit-argument mode forwards each group directly to pytest without adding these ignores (runner lines 168–175). This finding does not establish exclusion for bare pytest or explicitly targeted local tests.
25:

34: This is a source-supported conclusion, without runtime validation. CI configuration and deployed or installed versions are outside the supplied evidence; no claim is made about them. No material uncertainty remains for the inspected runner's root list and preset exclusion.

12: # Does the ordinary-preset exclusion of tests/local/ apply to explicit-argument invocation?
13: 
14: ## Question and scope
15: 
16: The earlier record, [Package runner test roots and local-test exclusion](../../research/2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md), concluded that `--loom-family` does not run `tests/local/`. The caller's condition has changed: no `--loom-family`; instead explicit arguments name `tests/local/test_example.py`. Can the earlier exclusion conclusion be applied to this call?
17: 
18: Scope: the minimal source snapshot in [provenance](../../../../provenance.json) (recorded commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`; remote freshness not checked). It is not a full checkout, deployment or CI evidence. The earlier record is preserved unchanged; this is a separately scoped revalidation for different invocation conditions. No tests or runner commands were executed.
19: 
20: ## Method and rationale
21: 
22: Static inspection of the runner's `main()` branch selection and the explicit-argument path, plus the test definitions for any coverage of that path. This is a single-source behavior question, so a direct source read suffices. Pytest's own collection semantics were not checked against documentation (no network access) and are flagged below as unverified background.
23: 
24: ## Findings
25: 
26: - **Observed in source:** the exclusion is not applied on the explicit path. `main()` enters the preset only when `argv[0] == "--loom-family"` ([runner](../../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 153–167). Otherwise it calls `split_groups(argv)` (lines 58–65, 168) and runs `subprocess.call([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", *group])` per group (lines 172–175). The tokens, including `tests/local/test_example.py`, are forwarded verbatim.
27: - The `local/` skipping lives only in `_tests_session` (lines 76–86, adds `--ignore=<local>`), `_shell_tests` (lines 88–95) and `_workflow_sessions` (lines 98–113). All are reached only through `loom_family_commands`, which the explicit path never calls. The nested-repository `--ignore` tokens (lines 123, 146–149) are likewise preset-only.
28: - The module docstring (lines 1–6, 7–9) describes `local/` skipping as a property of `--loom-family`, consistent with this reading.
29: - **Test definitions:** the `local` exclusion tests in [test_run_package_tests.py](../../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py) (lines 222–235, 285–298) use `loom_family_commands`/`only=` and therefore cover the preset only. The explicit-path tests (lines 16–36) check group splitting, exit codes and empty-argument handling; none targets a `local/` path. Read, not run.
30: - **Inference (not verified here):** with the runner adding no ignore, whether pytest collects the named file depends on pytest's behavior for explicitly given file arguments and on any pytest.ini/conftest in the real repository. From general pytest knowledge, an explicitly named file path is collected and `local` has no special meaning to pytest, so the file would most likely run. This was not confirmed against documentation or by execution.
31: - **Not established:** `tests/local/test_example.py` does not exist in the snapshot (only four source files were supplied), so its content, markers, skips or fixtures are unknown.
32: 
33: ## Evidence
34: 
35: | Claim | Source | Kind / conditions |
36: |---|---|---|
37: | Explicit mode forwards groups to pytest with no `local` ignore | [runner lines 153–175](../../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py) | Source inspection, snapshot at the commit recorded in provenance |
38: | `local` exclusion is implemented only inside preset helpers | runner lines 76–113, 123–149 | Source inspection; call graph traced from `main()` |
39: | No test covers explicit-path `local/` handling | [tests](../../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py) lines 16–36, 222–298 | Test definitions read, not run |
40: | Snapshot integrity | `fixture-observations.json` (harness observation, not my command): runner and test sha256 equal the values in provenance (`6730a53e…0d54`, `b7ed3d4e…da28`) | I did not recompute hashes |
41: | Fixture git state | Same file: `main` = `4959e62`, `research-fixture` = `00fa764` is an ancestor of `main`, no tags, no remotes | Harness observation of a temporary fixture only |
42: 
43: ## Decision impact
44: 
45: The earlier conclusion does **not** transfer. Its own limitation already said the exclusion is preset-specific and does not cover explicitly targeted local tests. For this change: do not rely on the runner to keep `tests/local/test_example.py` out of an explicit-argument call. By source, the runner would pass it to pytest, which (inference) would collect it. If the intent is to prevent local tests from running, the caller must not name them, or must add its own exclusion; if the intent is to run a local test deliberately, explicit arguments appear to be the route. The earlier decision (do not place tests meant for ordinary package coverage in `tests/local/`) is unaffected, since it concerns the preset.
46: 
47: ## Limitations and open questions
48: 
49: - No execution: whether pytest actually collects and runs the file is untested here, and pytest documentation was not consulted.
50: - Real repository ini/conftest settings, CI configuration, and deployed versions are outside the snapshot.
51: - The target file is absent from the fixture; its behavior is unknown.
52: - Explicit mode also lacks the nested-repository ignores; only relevant if an argument names a directory containing nested repositories.
53: - Revalidate if the runner source changes or if different arguments (e.g. caller-supplied `--ignore`, directory targets) are used.

14: ## Question and scope
15: 
16: The [earlier record](../../research/2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md) concluded that the ordinary `--loom-family` preset does not run `tests/local/`. The caller condition has changed: no `--loom-family`, and explicit arguments name `tests/local/test_example.py`. Can the earlier exclusion conclusion still be applied? The earlier record is retained unchanged as the basis for the `--loom-family` decision; this is a separately scoped revalidation for the active change `fixture-explicit-args`.
17: 
18: Scope: the supplied minimal source snapshot of the runner (attributed by [provenance](../../../../provenance.json) to commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`). Not a complete checkout, CI, or deployment. No tests or runner commands were executed.

20: ## Method and rationale
21: 
22: Reuse of the earlier record's evidence, with an applicability check, plus static inspection of the runner's `main` dispatch and `split_groups`, and the test definitions. This fits because the question is which code path handles the new invocation; no execution is needed or permitted.
23: 
24: ## Findings
25: 
26: - **Observed in source:** the earlier exclusion does not carry over. `main` enters the preset branch only when `argv[0] == "--loom-family"`. Any other argv goes to `split_groups`, then each group runs as `[sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", *group]` ([runner](../../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 153–176). The `local/` exclusion lives in `_tests_session`, `_shell_tests` and `_workflow_sessions` (lines 76–113), which are reached only through `loom_family_commands` (lines 116–150), called only from the preset branch (line 163).
27: - **Inference:** so for `run_package_tests.py tests/local/test_example.py`, the runner adds no `--ignore` for `tests/local/` and does not consult `TEST_ROOTS`. The explicit path is passed straight to pytest, so pytest would normally collect it if the file exists and matches its collection rules. Pytest behavior is not verified here, only inferred from the runner forwarding the argument.
28: - **Also absent in this mode:** the nested-repository/worktree `--ignore` entries (lines 123, 146–149). Those apply only to the preset.
29: - **Docstring consistency:** the module docstring says `local/` is skipped for the `--loom-family` surface and that tests outside the roots do not run. That describes the preset's inventory, not explicit arguments (lines 4–11).
30: - **Test definitions:** the local-exclusion tests (lines 222–235, 285–310 in [tests](../../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py)) target the discovery helpers and command lists. The explicit-mode tests (lines 17–35) cover only group splitting, exit codes and empty input. None asserts that an explicit `tests/local/...` path is excluded or included. These were read, not run.
31: - **Fixture state:** `tests/local/test_example.py` does not exist in this fixture, and only the minimal snapshot is present, so no collection claim about a real file is possible.
32: - **Harness observation (not run by me):** [fixture-observations.json](../../../../fixture-observations.json) records pre-run local git queries (`main` at `4959e62`, containing `research-fixture` at `00fa764`, no tags/remotes) and SHA256 values for the runner (`6730a53e…0d54`) and test file (`b7ed3d4e…da28`). These match provenance, so the inspected source is the same revision the earlier record analyzed. Git history was not otherwise mined.

46: The earlier "tests/local is not run" conclusion remains valid only for `--loom-family` and must not be applied to this invocation. Decisions that assume local tests are skipped here (for example, treating the call as safe because they are skipped) are unsupported. 11: # Claim boundary for sample receipt exit_code=0 and the package-test-roots record
12: 
13: ## Question and scope
14: 
15: Can the existing [sample receipt](../../../sample-receipt.json) (`exit_code: 0`) and the existing record [package test roots](2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md) support the claim "the whole package tests/CI pass for this snapshot and the source is traceable"? Scope: the temporary local fixture only (minimal source snapshot in `src/`, [provenance](../../../provenance.json)). No tests, remote queries, publishing or acceptance were performed or are implied. The existing record was not edited; this is a separate question from its test-root/`local/` question.
16: 
17: ## Method and rationale
18: 
19: Source and artifact inspection (receipt, existing record, provenance, runner source, test definitions) plus the harness-supplied [fixture observations](../../../fixture-observations.json) (git queries and SHA-256 values taken during fixture preparation, not by me). Sufficient to bound a claim; no execution needed or permitted. I had only file read/write tools, so I recomputed no hash and ran no git command.
20: 
21: ## Findings
22: 
23: Observed / source-supported:
24: 
25: - The receipt describes an authoring run of a `codex exec` agent (id `B02`, requested model, `elapsed_seconds` 42.6). Its `exit_code: 0` is that agent process's exit status. Its only recorded project change is `added_project_files: [docs/loom/research/2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md]`, with `source_unchanged: true`. It contains no pytest/runner command, test counts, or CI job. It says nothing about any test passing.
26: - The existing record states "no tests or runner commands were executed" and "source-supported conclusion, without runtime validation", and that CI and deployed versions are outside its evidence. It answers only: which roots are in `TEST_ROOTS` and that the `--loom-family` preset skips `local/`.
27: - The runner's `--loom-family` mode would run several groups (code, design, workflow-python/shell/mermaid, including `npm ci` and `node`). The snapshot holds 4 files only: no `loom-design/`, `loom-workflow/`, `tests/` other than one test file, no CI config, no `pytest.ini`/conftest. The package suite cannot be represented by this snapshot ([runner](../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 116–150).
28: - Test definitions in [the test file](../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py) were read, not run; they depend on helpers outside what I verified (e.g. `_seed_repo`, `REPO`).
29: 
30: Hash and provenance (harness observation, not my measurement):
31: 
32: - fixture-observations.json SHA-256 for the four source files equals the `provenance.json` entries (runner `6730a53e…0d54`, test `b7ed3d4e…0da28`, `repo_files.py` `62333168…6399`, `git_exec.py` `9c721b8e…e7c7`). Observed paths carry a `src/` prefix versus provenance paths (e.g. `scripts/run_package_tests.py`); this is a snapshot-layout mapping I infer, not stated in provenance.
33: - Provenance ties the files to original-repo HEAD `d5a7f0da…` and a locally recorded `origin/main` of the same value; `remote_freshness` is "not checked". The original repository path is outside this fixture and was not read.
34: - The record's SHA-256 (`c54f2872…1283`) was observed, but provenance has no entry for the record, so there is no independent expected hash for it. [snapshots/original-research.md](../../../snapshots/original-research.md) reads identically to the record by my inspection; I did not hash it.
35: - Git (observation file): `main` = `4959e62`, `research-fixture` = `00fa764` is an ancestor of `main`; no tags, no remotes; the record is in the temporary fixture's history, not the original project's.
36: - Links in the existing record (`../../../provenance.json`, `../../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py`, `../../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py`) resolve from `docs/loom/research/` to existing files. Cited line anchors broadly match, with small offsets (e.g. `TEST_ROOTS` is at line 53, the `code` group begins at 124, `_shell_tests` at 88–95); these do not change the conclusions. The record lacks the template's H1 heading (cosmetic).
37: 
38: ## Evidence
39: 
40: | Claim | Source kind | Status |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | exit_code 0 is an authoring-agent exit status | [receipt](../../../sample-receipt.json) command and fields | source inspection |
43: | No test or CI result exists | receipt, record, fixture-observations (no test command) | absence in inspected artifacts; not proof tests were never run elsewhere |
44: | Source files match provenance hashes | [observations](../../../fixture-observations.json) vs [provenance](../../../provenance.json) | harness observation, pre-actor; no post-write hash supplied |
45: | Runner/test content supports the root/`local/` claim | runner and test file | source inspection; tests not run |
46: 
47: ## Decision impact
48: 
49: Can claim (within the fixture, with attribution):
50: 
51: - Four snapshot source files match provenance hashes (per harness observation), and provenance names an original commit, with remote freshness unchecked.
52: - The record is a retained, source-inspection-based answer on `TEST_ROOTS` and `local/` exclusion in that snapshot, with working relative links.
53: - The receipt shows one authoring run exited 0 and added that one record.
54: 
55: Cannot claim:
56: 
57: - That the package tests or CI pass: no test was run, no result recorded, and the snapshot is too small for the suite. `exit_code: 0` is not a test result.
58: - That traceability is complete or verified against the original repository: the original repo, commit `d5a7f0da…`, and remote were not inspected; the fixture git history is temporary; the record has no independent hash.
59: - Deployment, installation, or release status.
60: 
61: To support the stronger claim you would need an actual recorded run of the intended test command on the full checkout at the named commit (with command, environment, result), plus CI evidence, which I did not obtain.
62: 
63: ## Limitations and open questions
64: 
65: - I recomputed no hash and ran no git command; hash and git facts come from the harness observation file, taken before my execution, with no post-write hash for the record.
66: - Whether the original tests pass at `d5a7f0da…` is unknown.
67: - The `src/` path mapping and the equivalence of the snapshot copy of the record are inferred from reading.
68: - Revalidate if the snapshot, provenance, or receipt changes.

11: # What can be claimed from the sample receipt and the package-test-roots record
12: 
13: ## Question and scope
14: 
15: The user intends to claim that this snapshot's whole package tests/CI pass and that its sources are traceable, based on `exit_code=0` in [sample-receipt.json](../../../sample-receipt.json) and the existing record [package test roots](2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md). Which parts are supported? Scope: the temporary local fixture only. No tests, remote queries or publishing were performed. This is a separate question from the earlier record, which is left unchanged.
16: 
17: ## Method and rationale
18: 
19: Inspection of existing artifacts (receipt, earlier record, provenance, harness observations, runner source), per the source policy: an exit code, an existing artifact or a test definition does not alone prove the promised outcome. No command could be run in this session; hash values below are harness observations, not my measurements.
20: 
21: ## Findings
22: 
23: 1. **Receipt does not show package tests ran.** The receipt (`id` B02) records a `codex exec ... -` invocation of a different executor (model `gpt-6.1-sol`), with `exit_code: 0`. That is the exit status of the executor process, not of `run_package_tests.py` or pytest. The command contains no runner invocation, and the receipt has no test output, counts or test command. Observed: the executor exited 0, `source_unchanged: true`, and it added one file, `docs/loom/research/2026-11-08-package-test-roots.md`. Its `-C` and `-o` paths point to a different directory than this fixture. No claim about any test result follows.
24: 2. **The research record is static source inspection only.** It states that no tests or runner commands were executed and that no runtime validation exists. File existence is not a test outcome.
25: 3. **The snapshot cannot support a whole-suite claim.** `src/` has 4 files: the runner, `repo_files.py`, `git_exec.py` and `test_run_package_tests.py`. The runner's `TEST_ROOTS` expects `tests`, `loom-code/tests`, `loom-design/tests` and `loom-workflow/tests`. Apart from this one test file, no listed test root is present, and the Mermaid group needs `loom-workflow/tests/mermaid`, which is absent. A full package run cannot be reproduced from this snapshot. The runner's `--loom-family` mode does not depend on a CI configuration, and CI config is not in the snapshot either. "CI passed" has no evidence.
26: 4. **Source traceability is partial.** Harness observation: SHA256 of the four `src/` files equals the values in [provenance.json](../../../provenance.json) (runner `6730a53e…`, `repo_files` `62333168…`, `git_exec` `9c721b8e…`, test file `b7ed3d4e…`), and the earlier record's hash statement matches these. Provenance ties them to commit `d5a7f0da…` of an external original repository; that repository was not readable and `remote_freshness` is "not checked". The locally recorded `origin/main` equals HEAD only as a recorded string. So hashes show the files match provenance's declaration, not that the commit exists or contains those contents.
27: 5. **Record accuracy.** I checked the earlier record's anchors against the runner and the test file: `TEST_ROOTS` at line 53 (record says 51–55, which includes adjacent lines), the `local/` ignore in `_tests_session` (76–86), shell exclusion (88–95), preset and explicit-argument modes (153–176). The test definitions at lines 222 and 285–311 assert root list and `local` exclusion. The record's narrow claim, that these roots are listed and the preset excludes `local/`, is supported by source. Line ranges are slightly loose (for example, the code group begins at 124, not 122).
28: 6. **Git state.** Harness observation of the local git queries: `main` is `4959e62`, `research-fixture` is `00fa764` and is an ancestor of `main`; no tags and no remotes. This is a temporary harness repository, not the original project history. The record's own SHA256 is `c54f2872…` (harness observation, pre-actor; the file was not modified by me). Observations carry no post-write actor-copy hash.
29:

40: 
41: ## Decision impact
42: 
43: Supportable claim: "In this fixture, the supplied runner source, by static reading, lists four test roots and its `--loom-family` preset excludes `local/`. The four snapshot files match the SHA256 values declared in provenance for commit `d5a7f0da…`; the original repository and remote freshness were not verified."
44: 
45: Not supportable: that the whole package tests pass, that CI passed, that the receipt shows any test run, or that provenance has been verified against the original repository. To claim a test result, someone must run the runner in a complete checkout, retain the command, output and revision, and have CI evidence if CI is claimed. I did not accept or approve the result on the user's behalf.
46:

51: - Whether the receipt's prompt asked for tests is unknown, as the prompt is not in the receipt.
52: - Runtime behavior of the runner (including `nested_repositories`) was not examined or executed.

     2	
     3	git is asked, not reimplemented: `git ls-files --cached --others
     4	--exclude-standard -z`, run through `git_exec.run_git` with `-C <root>`, so a
     5	root that is a subdirectory scopes the listing to that subtree. `-z` is
     6	mandatory -- without it a path containing a newline comes back shell-quoted
     7	(git-config(1), core.quotePath). Encoding/argv rationale lives in
     8	`git_exec.run_git`'s docstring and is not restated here.
     9	
    10	When there is no git the filesystem is walked instead, and a `.gitignore` that
    11	happens to be present is NOT honoured. ripgrep, fd and ruff all behave that way
    12	by default, and it keeps a `git archive` copy working. A BARE repository is git
    13	even though `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints nothing there; it owns no
    14	work tree, so it owns no files, and the walk must not be reached.
    15	
    16	"No git" is decided by `--show-toplevel` printing nothing, so a checkout whose
    17	git is NOT installed, or whose repository git refuses (for example
    18	`safe.directory` dubious ownership), is walked as well -- and that walk lists
    19	the files of any nested worktree again, which the git path would have
    20	dropped. This module does not tell those cases apart; `rehearse_probes.py`
    21	does, with an upward check for a `.git` marker.
    22	
    23	The two paths agree on a tree that holds no foreign subtree, not on every tree:
    24	without git, `_walk_entries` drops a nested repository's `.git` marker but still
    25	walks that subtree and returns every other file in it, whereas the git path
    26	drops the whole subtree as one opaque entry.
    27	
    28	Both paths then drop any path with a component in IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES, and
    29	drop every entry that is not an existing regular file: `--others` emits a
    30	nested repository or linked worktree as one opaque directory entry such as
    31	`wt/` rather than its files -- that entry is how the worktree's contents stay
    32	out of the listing, so it is dropped, never expanded -- and `--cached` still
    33	lists a staged-but-deleted path. Paths returned are absolute; every caller
    34	derives its own relative form.
    35	
    36	Submodule contents are never listed: `--recurse-submodules` is documented as
    37	incompatible with `--others` (git-ls-files(1)).
    38	
    39	`nested_worktrees` and `nested_repositories` answer the neighbouring git
    40	question -- where the foreign subtrees inside this root are -- for the callers
    41	that must exclude those paths rather than list files themselves, so that no
    42	second git invocation grows outside this module. They are not the same set:
    43	`nested_repositories` names the opaque directory entries git collapsed, which
    44	covers a clone and a submodule but misses a gitignored worktree;
    45	`nested_worktrees` names what `git worktree list` reports, which covers the
    46	gitignored worktree but nothing else. A caller that must exclude everything
    47	foreign takes the union.
    48	
    49	Sibling-module import (no `__init__.py`), following `git_exec`'s own
    50	precedent in this directory.
    51	"""
    52	from __future__ import annotations
    53	
    54	import os
    55	from pathlib import Path
    56	
    57	from git_exec import run_git
    58	
    59	IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES = frozenset(
    60	    {".git", ".pytest_cache", "__pycache__", "node_modules"}
    61	)
    62	
    63	
    64	def repository_files(root: Path | str) -> list[Path]:
    65	    """Absolute paths of the files belonging to the repository at `root`."""
    66	    root = Path(root)
    67	    entries = _git_entries(root)
    68	    if entries is None:
    69	        entries = _walk_entries(root)
    70	    return [path for path in entries if path.is_file()]
    71	
    72	
    73	def nested_worktrees(root: Path | str) -> list[Path]:
    74	    """Absolute paths of the git worktrees that live inside `root`.
    75	
    76	    `git worktree list --porcelain -z` lists every worktree of the repository,
    77	    including the one `root` itself is in; only the ones strictly below `root`
    78	    are returned, so the repository's own worktree is never one of them. The
    79	    paths git prints are already resolved, so `root` is resolved before the
    80	    comparison. No git, or a `root` outside any repository, is an empty list,
    81	    not an error -- the callers have nothing to exclude in that case. `-z`
    82	    NUL-terminates each field, so a path holding a newline stays one path
    83	    (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree, git >= 2.36).
    84	    """
    85	    root = Path(root).resolve()
    86	    listing = run_git(root, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain", "-z", strip=False)
    87	    if listing is None:
    88	        return []
    89	    paths = [
    90	        Path(field[len("worktree "):])
    91	        for field in listing.split("\0")
    92	        if field.startswith("worktree ")
    93	    ]
    94	    return sorted(path for path in paths if path != root and root in path.parents)
    95	
    96	
    97	def nested_repositories(root: Path | str) -> list[Path]:
    98	    """Absolute paths of the git repositories nested inside `root`.
    99	
   100	    These are exactly the entries `repository_files` drops as "not a file":
   101	    git collapses a nested repository -- a linked worktree, a plain clone
   102	    dropped in `vendor/`, a submodule's gitlink -- to one opaque directory
   103	    entry instead of listing its contents. Naming them lets a caller that
   104	    must EXCLUDE those subtrees (rather than list files) use the same answer
   105	    the scanners use. No git here is an empty list, not an error.
   106	
   107	    A symlink is excluded even when it points at a directory: git records it
   108	    as a symlink blob (mode 120000), never as a collapsed subtree, and
   109	    `is_dir` alone follows it -- naming it would make a caller exclude the
   110	    real directory it points at. `not is_symlink()` is preferred over
   111	    requiring a `.git` marker inside because a gitlink whose submodule is
   112	    not checked out is still an empty real directory git collapsed.
   113	    """
   114	    root = Path(root)
   115	    entries = _git_entries(root)
   116	    if entries is None:
   117	        return []
   118	    return sorted(
   119	        {path for path in entries if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink()}
   120	    )
   121	
   122	
   123	def _git_entries(root: Path) -> list[Path] | None:
   124	    """Paths git lists under `root`, or None when there is no git here.
   125	
   126	    A bare repository is git, but owns no work tree: `--show-toplevel` has
   127	    nothing to print there, so absence of git is decided by
   128	    `--is-bare-repository` FIRST -- otherwise the walk fallback would return
   129	    the object store itself (`HEAD`, `config`, `hooks/*.sample`), whose
   130	    directory is named `foo.git` and so prunes nothing.
   131	    """
   132	    if run_git(root, "rev-parse", "--is-bare-repository") == "true":
   133	        return []
   134	    if not run_git(root, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"):
   135	        return None
   136	    listing = run_git(
   137	        root, "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z",
   138	        strip=False,
   139	    )
   140	    if listing is None:
   141	        return None
   142	    return [
   143	        root / entry
   144	        for entry in listing.split("\0")
   145	        if entry and not _is_ignored(Path(entry).parts)
   146	    ]
   147	
   148	
   149	def _walk_entries(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
   150	    """Every file under `root`, minus the ignored names.
   151	
   152	    Pruning `subdirectories` is the cheap half -- it keeps the walk out of
   153	    the subtree. The filename is filtered too, because an ignored name is
   154	    not always a directory: a linked worktree and a submodule both mark
   155	    their directory with a `.git` FILE. Filtering only directories is what
   156	    made this path disagree with the git path on the same tree.
   157	    """
   158	    paths: list[Path] = []
   159	    for directory, subdirectories, filenames in os.walk(root):
   160	        subdirectories[:] = [
   161	            name for name in subdirectories
   162	            if name not in IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES
   163	        ]
   164	        paths.extend(
   165	            Path(directory) / name for name in filenames
   166	            if name not in IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES
   167	        )
   168	    return paths
   169	
   170	
   171	def _is_ignored(parts) -> bool:
   172	    return any(part in IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES for part in parts)

     2	
     3	`run_git` is the one git-invocation body in this directory: the
     4	return/raise shape it hands back is selected entirely by its `check` and
     5	`text` parameters, so the three failure shapes its callers used to
     6	hand-roll independently live here instead. It was extracted from six
     7	wrappers around `git -C <repo> ...`, five of which were deleted with the
     8	pre-1.0 script families at loom-code 1.0; `loom_checker.py` is the caller
     9	that remains. This docstring is the SSOT for the encoding/argv rationale
    10	below -- a module that wraps `run_git` points back here rather than
    11	restating it. Direct `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` calls that were never
    12	one of those wrappers still exist (`check_doc_citations.py`); they keep
    13	their own encoding behavior, and routing them here is a separate change,
    14	not something this module claims to have done.
    15	
    16	Encoding: `encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape"` is passed explicitly
    17	rather than the locale-dependent default `text=True` picks up
    18	(locale.getencoding(), fixed at THIS interpreter's startup from
    19	LC_ALL/LANG -- not the child's). git's own path output is raw bytes that
    20	are valid UTF-8 whenever core.quotePath is left at its default
    21	(quoted/escaped otherwise; git-config(1)) -- decoding as UTF-8
    22	unconditionally, with surrogateescape to still tolerate a stray non-UTF-8
    23	byte, keeps a non-ASCII path from raising UnicodeDecodeError under a
    24	non-UTF-8 process locale. `encoding=`/`errors=` are applied ONLY when
    25	text=True: passing them at all -- even under text=False -- forces
    26	subprocess.run into text mode regardless, which would hand a `text=False`
    27	caller (e.g. a raw-bytes `git show` read) a `str` where it requires raw
    28	`bytes`.
    29	
    30	argv is handed to the child as UTF-8 `bytes`, not `str`: on POSIX,
    31	subprocess encodes `str` arguments with the filesystem encoding
    32	(os.fsencode -- PEP 383), which is ASCII under an uncoerced C/POSIX
    33	locale, so a repo-relative path such as `src/日本.py` inside a git argument
    34	would otherwise raise UnicodeEncodeError before git ever ran (observed on
    35	a Linux CI runner; macOS's filesystem encoding is always UTF-8, which is
    36	why it did not reproduce locally). git itself treats paths as bytes, so
    37	UTF-8 bytes are exactly what it expects regardless of the process locale
    38	(git-config(1) core.quotePath describes the same byte-level model on
    39	output).
    40	
    41	Sibling-module import (no `__init__.py`, no conftest), following the
    42	existing `import distribute` precedent in this same scripts/ directory.
    43	"""
    44	from __future__ import annotations
    45	
    46	import subprocess
    47	from pathlib import Path
    48	
    49	
    50	def run_git(
    51	    repo: Path,
    52	    *args: str,
    53	    timeout: float | None = None,
    54	    check: bool = False,
    55	    text: bool = True,
    56	    strip: bool = True,
    57	):
    58	    """Run `git -C <repo> <*args>` and return its shape per `check`/`text`.
    59	
    60	    check=False: stripped stdout, or None on OSError / non-zero exit /
    61	    TimeoutExpired. check=True: raises exactly what
    62	    `subprocess.run(check=True)` raises (CalledProcessError on non-zero
    63	    exit); OSError / TimeoutExpired propagate. text=False: raw bytes, no
    64	    strip regardless of `strip`. strip=False: unstripped stdout.
    65	    """
    66	    argv = ["git", "-C", str(repo), *args]
    67	    argv_bytes = [
    68	        arg.encode("utf-8", "surrogateescape") if isinstance(arg, str) else arg
    69	        for arg in argv
    70	    ]
    71	    text_kwargs = {"encoding": "utf-8", "errors": "surrogateescape"} if text else {}
    72	    try:
    73	        result = subprocess.run(
    74	            argv_bytes, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout, check=check,
    75	            text=text, **text_kwargs,
    76	        )
    77	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    78	        if check:
    79	            raise
    80	        return None
    81	
    82	    if not check and result.returncode != 0:
    83	        return None
    84	
    85	    stdout = result.stdout
    86	    if text and strip:
    87	        stdout = stdout.strip()
    88	    return stdout

    10	
    11	## Question and scope
    12	
    13	Which directories does this runner list in `TEST_ROOTS`, and does its ordinary package suite include `tests/local/`? This informs placement of a new plugin's tests. Scope is the supplied minimal source snapshot, attributed by [provenance](../../provenance.json) to commit `d5a7f0da247214bdb9c61fe90c550256432e5f76`; it is neither a complete checkout nor evidence of deployment.
    14	
    15	## Method and rationale
    16	
    17	Static source inspection of the runner's entry point and discovery helpers, with relevant test definitions as corroboration. This directly answers the single-source question; no tests or runner commands were executed.
    18	
    19	## Findings and evidence
    20	
    21	- `TEST_ROOTS` contains exactly `tests`, `loom-code/tests`, `loom-design/tests`, and `loom-workflow/tests` ([runner](../../src/scripts/run_package_tests.py), lines 51–55).
    22	- The package preset is selected by `--loom-family` (lines 153–167). Its `code` group includes the first two roots and calls `_tests_session` (lines 122–128). That helper excludes the root's `local/` while checking for tests and adds `--ignore=<absolute local path>` when present (lines 76–86). Consequently, `tests/local/` is excluded from this preset's Python collection. Shell discovery likewise excludes each root's direct `local/` subtree (lines 89–96). Design and workflow Python paths also exclude their root-level `local/` directories (lines 99–114, 129–132).
    23	- [Test definitions](../../src/tests/test_run_package_tests.py), lines 222–235, 285–310, assert the root list and exclusion of Python and shell files under `tests/local/`. These definitions were read, not run.
    24	- The exclusion is preset-specific: the alternate explicit-argument mode forwards each group directly to pytest without adding these ignores (runner lines 168–175). This finding does not establish exclusion for bare pytest or explicitly targeted local tests.
    25	
    26	The inspected runner and test file SHA256 values, measured with `shasum -a 256`, match their entries in provenance: `6730a53e11d862d5d3d93eadcdafb2011b81f2595332e4a57ae49a504f660d54` and `b7ed3d4e19fd4d03c68df5d8ca796d03442a859874745564c20ddaeb7780da28`, respectively.
    27	
    28	## Decision impact
    29	
    30	Do not place tests intended for ordinary package coverage in `tests/local/`. A new standalone plugin test root is not automatically discovered: it must be added to `TEST_ROOTS`; otherwise use an existing listed root outside its excluded `local/` subtree, subject to the runner's normal discovery rules.
    31	
    32	## Limitations and open questions
    33	
    34	This is a source-supported conclusion, without runtime validation. CI configuration and deployed or installed versions are outside the supplied evidence; no claim is made about them. No material uncertainty remains for the inspected runner's root list and preset exclusion.
